newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Li Yung-chung, the suspected heroin trafficker, should stand trial here on bribery charges, the House Justice and Human Rights Committee decided yesterday. Li, cleared for extradition to the United States by the Criminal Court, has made allegations that have damaged the standing of the country and the judiciary in particular. (BANGKOK POST)

- The charter draft vetting committee has agreed to the media's demand that it remove a provision requiring the establishment of a commission on ethics in journalism. Committee spokesman says Article 40 of the draft constitution will be deleted because there will be problems enforcing its findings. Article 40 probihits employees of newspapers and other media from violating ethics to be set by an "independent" body which will have been set up by law. (THE NATION)

- The cabinet is to arrange a 2.5 billion baht fund designed to attract badly-needed financing for Hopewell (Thailand) Co's delayed mass transit project. The syndicated loan is part of a parcel approved yesterday to salvage the Bangkok project, which has made little headway in recent months. Transport and Communications minister says he expects the project to be completed ahead of the Asian Games in Bangkok in December next year. (BANGKOK POST)

- Bankers have agreed to lower interest rates by 50 basis points in the second round of rate cuts this year, as soon as the Bank of Thailand moves to reduce its discount rate. The agreement was made at a meeting of the Thai Bankers' Association yesterday. Central bank governor will make a final decision this week. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- An excise tax of 10 percent will be imposed on some environmentally-damaging products in a bid to alleviate the government's projected revenue shortfall in the 1997 fiscal year. The cabinet yesterday approved changes in excise tax covering nine product categories. The tax adjustments will increase government revenue by 7.739 billion baht each year, apart from simplifying the tax structure. (BUSINESS DAY)
